relations.statement: For c : Code and n : ℕ, v ∈ Code.eval c n iff there exists a halting TM0 configuration cfg reachable from initCfg0 (encode (n)) under M0 whose output tape reads the encoding of v.
relations.hypotheses: M0 is the TM0 machine obtained from the TM2to1 and TM1to0 compilations of the universal machine for c; encoding of input and output is fixed; no assumptions declared.

lemmas.statement: v ∈ Code.eval c n ↔ ∃ cfg, Reaches (TM0.step M0) (initCfg0 n') cfg ∧ halted cfg ∧ tapeOutput cfg = enc v

near_misses.claim: Using TM2to1.tr_eval alone gives only an existential statement about the halting tape and does not identify the tape contents with the encoding of v.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The tape content must be determined exactly as the encoded value in Code.eval c n, not merely exist.

open_obligations: Locate the declarations for M0, M1, G1, and the TM1to0 and TM2to1 correctness lemmas; they are not listed in @SRC or @KNOWN+, so none are cited.
Define the output-tape decoding for TM0 configurations.
Compose tr_eval across the TM2 to TM1 to TM0 stages with an explicit tape form.
Prove both directions of the iff, including the halting-iff-eval-nonempty direction.
Replace the placeholder lemma skeleton with a real Lean statement.
